The RCB3's with the U1 and U2 failures may have failed because of a power surge on the POE Cat6 ethernet cable.  The POE switch may have been powered up when the RCB3s were  connected.  The POE switch should be powered down when connecting devices.  The Dart failure may have been a hardware failure of the module, with no root cause.

One had the C13_POE broken off the PCB, as reported by the installer.  This failure could have occurred at the manufacturer or by the installer because of rough handling.  One has a U1_POE short. The RCB3's with the U1 and U2 failures may have failed because of a power surge on the POE Cat6 ethernet cable.  The POE switch may have been powered up when the RCB3s were connected which can cause this type failure.  The POE switch should be powered down when connecting devices.  The Dart failure may have been a hardware failure of the module, with no root cause. investigation_details: John Fetzner power-up and boot tested all 7 returned devices (11/16/2021): one RCB2 failed boot with a CRC error, one RCB2 had the manufacturing image and passed FCT, and the other five had 3.9.100 firmware. Steve Moore (12/21/2021) found no problems on six devices; one GAS needed touchscreen calibration and clicked with one RJ45 cable but was fine after a cable change. On iob-0241924vwis the kernel.bin differed from the release image by a few bytes, enough to fail the CRC, with no sign of an update attempt; a re-image fixes it. Lab results are attached (https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/browse/RCA-931#icft=RCA-931 returns lab test results-1.xlsx, 1/19/2022).
verification_summary: Record-review verification summary: Based on the existing Jira investigation, root-cause, review, and comment records. This summary documents previously recorded evidence; no new functional testing or independent verification was performed.

Laboratory inspection of the seven returned devices identified a CRC/kernel corruption failure on RCB2 iob-0241924vwis; a flash-memory cause was suggested but not confirmed. The other devices did not reproduce the reported failures in the documented software review, with one touchscreen/cable concern noted. Re-imaging was proposed for the corrupted device, and a replacement order was recorded. The record supports completion of the returned-device investigation, but does not establish completion of re-image validation, replacement installation or site acceptance testing. No-fault-found findings must not be represented as proof that the original site complaint was corrected. Basis: Investigation Details, Root Cause Summary and November 2021–February 2022 comments.

description: On 02/05, 6W Staff at UVA Medical Center reported that the touchscreen functionality of the GRS10 was intermittently not working. When I evaluated the GRS10, it appeared to be functional but occasionally would have to press a button a few times to get it to register. The top-right of the screen, specifically where the Wait List icon, would not register a press, and would instead register a touch to the Rooms Disabled button directly under it. 

 

WinSCP was installed on the Enterprise server and the pointercal file was removed, and the GRS10 was rebooted. When the GRS10's calibration screen came up, the upper-right corner of the screen still gave issues with registering a press, but it did go through after a few attempts. When the GRS10 screen came up to the Calls screen, the general functionality of the screen had improved, but the upper-right part was still not working. The 6W staff opted to use Menu > Wait List to get to the Wait List as a workaround.

 

The following day on 02/06, the staff reported the screen was completely unusable. They could not identify at what point in time the screen functionality degraded. I came onsite and verified that the screen was not operable. We replaced the GRS10 and the new GRS10 is working as intended. 

 

UVA has requested this GRS10 be sent in to be evaluated by R&D to understand why the initial issues with the screen started, and why the screen degraded further after removing the pointercal file.

A replacement GRS10 was ordered for the site and the faulty unit was returned for evaluation, which was completed with the root cause recorded in the ticket. The unit was replaced and the troubleshooting activities were captured in a knowledge base article covering inoperable touch screens on GRS10 or GRS5 devices.

description: At Cleveland Clinic Weston, version 3.9.102, @Christopher Skotnicki reported the following:

root_cause_summary: Base device process staff assignments to patient as staff assignments to locations, where primary caregiver always processes changes first resulting in blank secondary caregiver details when a primary is changed to secondary in Smart Client.
investigation_details: Digging deeper into this issue - particularly the test step in the attached document where a caregiver with a secondary role is switched to the primary role - I have found the reason for this issue.   Keep in mind the following about base devices:

1) They deal only in staff to location assignments.  Staff to patient assignments are given to base devices as staff to location assignments.

2) They deal only in the fact that a staff is assigned to a location, not any other details such as primary or secondary caregiver.

**When you hit save in smart client, for each staff member, this is the order of processing:**

1) modifications to the primary roles are sent out first.

2) modifications to the secondary roles are sent out next.

3) modifications to other roles are sent next, but this is not relevant to this case.

**So when you change a staff member from primary to secondary in the same location, this happens:**

1) removal of primary assignment - base device deletes that assignment.

2) addition of secondary assignment - base device adds that assignment.

This is all good and it works.  The staff shows up on the call details screen.

**When you change a staff member from secondary to primary in the same location, this happens:**

1) addition of primary assignment - causes no change on the base side because that assignment already exists.

2) removal of secondary assignment - base device deletes the assignment.

Since the staff to location assignment no longer exists on the base side, they disappear from the call details screen.

impact_description: IMPACT ASSESSMENT SUMMARY - impact assessment.
Under concurrent ADT admits for the same MRN, two admit requests could each pass a service-layer "is this MRN unique?" check and then both insert, producing two active Patient rows for a single MRN. Once duplicated, every subsequent update AND discharge for that MRN failed, leaving the patient permanently stuck in the system. Root cause was a time-of-check/time-of-use race: the uniqueness check and the insert were separate, non-atomic operations, so two callers could interleave between the check and the write. The fix moves uniqueness enforcement out of the service layer and into the database so the check and the write are a single atomic, serialized operation.

Uniqueness is enforced inside the stored procs (Patient_Insert_55, Patient_Update_55). Same-MRN callers are serialized with a SQL application lock, and uniqueness is re-verified atomically immediately before the write, so a duplicate admit is rejected cleanly. Discharge is deliberately never blocked by the uniqueness logic, so a patient already in a duplicated state can still be discharged.  Exception: MRN is already in use by another patient!
 thrown at PatientDAL.cs:234.
- The Inactivate path (used by both HL7 A03 and Admin Client manual discharge)
 calls Update internally, so it also fails, wrapped as
 ApplicationException: Unable to mark patient as deleted.
- Voalte Admin Client surfaces this to clinicians as the generic toast
 "Your action could not be completed. Try again after a few moments or
 contact your Technical Support Team."
- The system remains in this stuck state indefinitely — the defect is not
 self-correcting. Mirth retries continue to fail. Manual UI clicks continue
 to fail. The patient cannot be discharged from Voalte through any in-product
 path.
```
expected_results: ```
- At most one active Patient row exists for any given MRN at any time.
- One of the two concurrent admit operations succeeds end-to-end (creates the
  Patient row, creates the location assignment).
- The other concurrent operation fails fast with a deterministic error that
  ADTIntegrationService can surface as a FaultException, allowing Mirth to NACK
  the duplicate ADT message back to the HIS.
- Subsequent ADT updates and Admin Client discharge attempts for the affected
  patient succeed.
- No manual SQL intervention is required.
```
work_around: Manual SQL cleanup by Tech Support / customer DBA. Procedure documented in 
RCA-1820, Section 4.3:
 1\. Identify the duplicate Patient rows for the affected MRN (pre-flight 
 queries inspect dbo.Patient, dbo.PatientLocationAssignment, 
 dbo.StaffPatientApplicationRoleAssignment, dbo.PatientNote). 
 2\. In a single transaction, set IsActive = 0 on the duplicate Patient rows, 
 close all active PatientLocationAssignment rows 
 (EffectiveThru = SYSUTCDATETIME()), close all active staff-patient 
 assignments (EffectiveThruUtc = SYSUTCDATETIME()), and inactivate any 
 active patient notes. 
 3\. Verify dbo.Patient_UniqueMRN(, ) returns 0 before 
 COMMIT.

investigation_details: ````
The customer reported one patient (Same MRN ) appearing in two rooms simultaneously in Voalte Admin Client at UPMC Pinnacle West Shore (NC 4.1.200): PatientID `337242` in Room 549 (LocationID `2185`) and PatientID `337243` in Room 547 (LocationID `2246`). Manual discharge from Voalte Admin Client failed with the generic toast "Your action could not be completed." HL7 ADT messages from the customer's EMR for this patient were also being silently rejected.
We pulled the customer's `AdvancedServiceLogs - UPMC Westshore.zip` archive (110 MB) and traced the failure end-to-end:

impact_description: IMPACT ASSESSMENT SUMMARY - impact assessment.
Under concurrent ADT admits for the same MRN, two admit requests could each pass a service-layer "is this MRN unique?" check and then both insert, producing two active Patient rows for a single MRN. Once duplicated, every subsequent update AND discharge for that MRN failed, leaving the patient permanently stuck in the system. Root cause was a time-of-check/time-of-use race: the uniqueness check and the insert were separate, non-atomic operations, so two callers could interleave between the check and the write. The fix moves uniqueness enforcement out of the service layer and into the database so the check and the write are a single atomic, serialized operation.
Before: 
The PatientService data-access layer (PatientDAL) called a C# pre-check (Patient.IsUniqueMrn / IsUniqueAccountNumber) and then, in a separate step, executed the insert/update stored proc. Two concurrent same-MRN admits could both pass the pre-check before either inserted, so both rows were written.
After: 
Uniqueness is enforced inside the stored procs (Patient_Insert_55, Patient_Update_55). Same-MRN callers are serialized with a SQL application lock, and uniqueness is re-verified atomically immediately before the write, so a duplicate admit is rejected cleanly. Discharge is deliberately never blocked by the uniqueness logic, so a patient already in a duplicated state can still be discharged. The user-facing error is unchanged (same PatientMRNNotUnique / PatientAccountNumberNotUnique message), so callers see the same behavior on a rejected duplicate as before. The now-unused C# pre-check helpers were removed.

No. Changes are confined to the Patient admit/update/discharge path (two stored procedures and the PatientService data-access layer). summary: ADT INFO will admit patient when they have no location
description: an ADT INFO action can result in a patient being admitted if they are not active in our system.  Prior to August 2021, and after March of 2019, there was a check for a valid location prior to allowing an INFO to admit a patient.   
Some EMR systems will send an A08 prior to an A01 /ADMIT as part of their workflow.  Often the A08/INFO does not have location information as that comes later with the A01.  What we end up with is the A08 causing the patient to be admitted with no location and then the A01 gets rejected because the patient is already active and we reject all A01/ADMIT for an already active patient to avoid double admission.  Now, we’ve got essentially orphaned patients with no location and no easy way to discharge them. 

---

## Task Description

* GOAL: Fix code that prevents an ADT-A01 (ADMIT) from processing due to a previous ADT-A08 (INFO) having already been processed.
* BACKGROUND: A change to the `PatientStaffService` was made so that when an ADT-A08 is processed it will perform an ADMIT action (TACO-5406). However, some hospital EMR’s use an ADT-A08 as a “Pre-Admit” (instead of using an ADT-A04. In these hospitals they will send an ADT-A08 then later send an ADT-A01.  
    
  The processing of ADT messages can be complicated due to the business rules that we have implemented. Currently, when the ADT-A01 comes across it first checks to see if the “Master Patient ID” is “active” and if it is then it logs a message (“An active patient is already admitted at location…) and continues – basically ignoring the admit (“dropping it on the floor”).

  \# 1. Augment the call to Patient.IsMasterPatientIdActive to include the location or action

The proposed handling was to treat an incoming A01 admit as a transfer when the patient is already present in Nurse Call for any reason, and to ignore an A08 information update as a pre-admission message when it has no PV1 assigned location and the patient is not active in the database. A field workaround of altering the Mirth ADT channel to set the actionType to XFER when it resolves to ADMIT was proposed but flagged as needing validation on all versions from 4.1.000 and as risking loss of configured patient risks when Nurse Call receives a transfer. The issue was reported live at a customer with a patient safety concern, an RCA was opened, and the upgrade team sought a way to assess which customers would be affected; the code change broke several automated tests that were fixed and re-executed, and all planned tests eventually passed.

It is agreed that direct tests are sufficient and regression tests should include patient persistence tests (risks, notes, patient information), Patient/Staff Assignment tests and any admission test with A01, A08, A60 and A13 messages.

steps_taken: Update an inactive patient using the EMR without assigning a location.  Admit the patient using the EMR.
actual_results: The admission is rejected because the A08 caused that patient that patient to become active.
expected_results: The patient will be admitted
work_around: Workaround: To get the patients back in the bed, take the last A08 (update message), turning it into an A03 (discharge, copying MSH-7 date/time for PV1-45 discharge date/time) and then turning that A03 into an A13 (cancel discharge).   
(convert the messages into discharge and then convert it into a cancel discharge, we can then admit the patient)
